newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Amnesty says Colombia's rights pledge rings hollow.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty says Colombia's rights pledge rings hollow.

text.p: Amnesty International accused the Colombian government on Wednesday of making empty promises to defend human rights in the light of the murder of a leftist politician last weekend.

"This latest assassination makes the public commitment undertaken by the Colombian government in relation to improving human rights sound more and more like empty rhetoric," the London-based rights group said in a communique.

Josue Giraldo, a member of the opposition Patriotic Union party (UP), said to be the political arm of Colombia's main guerrilla force, was shot dead by an unidentified gunman in Villavicencio, east of Bogota, early on Sunday.
The killer has not yet been captured but Amnesty said the shooting appeared to be the work of a right-wing paramilitary group working in league with the security forces.

Besides being a UP leader, Giraldo was also a member of the Civic Committee for Human Rights in eastern Meta province. Four committee heads were murdered in 1992 and Giraldo had received numerous threats in the past.

"We called on the authorities to guarantee the security of human rights workers in Colombia... if that had been done Giraldo would not be dead. The government has pledged to eradicate paramilitary groups, who in cooperation with the security forces carry out these abuses but not a single step has been taken," Amnesty wrote.
More than two thousand UP members have been killed by suspected paramilitaries since the party's formation in 1985.

Colombia has one of the worst human rights records in Latin America and Amnesty says violations have increased under President Ernesto Samper because of his inability to rein in extremist political forces.
Presidential human rights advisers were unavailable for comment on the Amnesty communique on Wednesday.
